- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows divergence from price trend, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits strong lag in downward corrections — when true price drops sharply, forecast often remains high for 3–5 days; apply a “lagged decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until trend stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment is high, reduce forecast volatility; if sentiment is low, allow more mean-reversion pressure.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture sentiment-driven reversals; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.5, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 days.
